full_judgment:
7. Mr. Omar Faroque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff petitioner submits that the Court of appeal below as final Court of fact fails to consider that on the admitted position of the parties the suit is not barred by limitation. He further submits that the Court of appeal below on surmises held that the plaintiff had knowledge of the deed of gift from before. He further submits that the Court of appeal below did not at all consider that the donor Gurajan did not acquire any property from her second husband as Anar Ali, second husband of Gurajan divorced her 3 years before his death. 

 9. Where a gift has been challenged it is to be seen as to whether the conditions for a valid gift has been full filed. The conditions for a valid gift are (i) offer (ii) acceptance and (iii) delivery of possession. If any one of these conditions lacking the gift itself stands as void. From the deposition of the witnesses I find that witness No. 1 for the plaintiff ascertained that he is in possession of the suit land. P.Ws.2, 3 and 4 corroborated P.W.1 as to his possession over the suit land. On the other hand, D.W.1 in his deposition stated that due to affection, his mother gifted the property to him. He further stated that his father, second husband of Gurajan divorced her mother 3 years before his death. He further stated that his mother inherited one Kani, 7 gonda lands from his father as wife. Out of this land, her mother got 17 gondas of land as heir of his father. Out of these 17 gondas of lands 15 gondas of land she gifted to him. D.W.2 and 3 did not say any word as to possession of the suit land. It is an absurd proposition that divorcee wife inherited any thing from her ex-husband. The defendant No. l's whole case is that her mother inherited the properties from her divorce husband which is not correct. A divorced wife does not inherit anything from her ex-husband. Question of inheritance by wife come after death of husband. So the claim of the defendant No.1 that her mother got the property from her second husband by inheritance is a myth. The Court of appeal below found that the suit is barred by limitation. The Court of appeal below foolishly held without knowing or considering the facts disclosed by the parties. From perusal of the Judgment of the Court of appeal below I find that the learned Subordinate Judge did not discussed the evidence on record nor he gave any good reasons for his decision. It is to be borne in mind that this is a suit for declaration that deed of gift has been obtained fraudulently. No one of the defendant witnesses have stated that defendant No.1 is in possession of the suit land. Limitation does not apply against a person who proved possession in the disputed land. A gift is valid if the aforesaid 3 conditions have been fulfilled. If one of the condition is absent the gift itself is not valid. As such the question that the suit is barred by limitation does not arise because the plaintiff has been able to prove that he is in possession of the suit land all through rendering the gift itself as not been acted upon. A deed if not acted upon the period of limitation of such deed cannot be considered to shut down legitimate claim of a claiment. The Court of appeal below while allowing the appeal did not consider this factum that gift was not acted upon. The Court of appeal below further failed to consider that the predecessor-in-interest of the defendant No.1 i.e. the donor did not acquire any property from her second husband as he divorced her mother. When the donor or transferor acquired no title whatever deed of transfer, either by way of sale or by way of gift or, by way of will, cannot confer any title to a transferee or a donee. I find the judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge is devoid of any substance. The learned Subordinate Judge does not know how to reverse a judgment. Even he did not consider the depositions and exhibits filed by the parties.
